title: Interview Prep and Senior Leadership
tagline: Convert knowledge into offers: portfolio, behavioral stories, ML/agent case rounds, senior-level scope.

topics.title: Portfolio and proof of work
items: Build and ship an agent product end to end with evals, tracing and a public write-up
Implement a mini transformer / GPT from scratch
Build a RAG system with measured retrieval quality and an eval harness
Deploy a model with vLLM on Kubernetes with autoscaling and dashboards
Contribute to an open-source AI project (frameworks, evals, MCP servers)
Write 3 deep technical posts about problems you solved
Keep a quantified impact list: latency, cost, quality, adoption numbers
questions: Which project best shows your depth and what would you do differently?

topics.title: Technical round types
topics.summary: Know the formats and prepare for each.
items: Coding round: Python, medium-level DSA, clean code
Practical coding: build an agent loop / tool-calling / RAG pipeline live
ML fundamentals deep-dive: transformers, training, optimization
LLM application case study: debug a failing RAG or agent
System design round: classic and AI-specific
Eval design round: design metrics and datasets for a given product
Take-home: scoped project with write-up
Past project deep dive: architecture, decisions, failures, metrics
Research paper discussion: read and critique recent papers
questions: Implement a minimal ReAct agent without any framework in 30 minutes.
Here's a transcript of a failing agent run. Diagnose it.

topics.title: Behavioral and senior-scope stories
topics.summary: Seniors are hired for judgement, ownership and influence.
items: STAR stories: conflict, failure, ambiguity, tight deadline, mentoring
A story where you changed technical direction with data
A story about a production incident you owned
A story about saying no / pushing back on scope
A story about delivering a cross-team project
Leading design reviews and writing design docs
Mentoring and raising team standards
Product sense: tie technical choices to user and business outcomes
Communicating uncertainty and risk to non-technical stakeholders
questions: Tell me about a time an AI feature you shipped failed in production.
How do you decide whether to build an AI feature at all?

topics.title: Staying current
topics.summary: The field moves monthly. Build a lightweight, sustainable habit.
items: Weekly: skim 3 primary sources (arXiv sanity, provider changelogs, engineering blogs)
Monthly: read one paper deeply and implement the key idea
Follow: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Hugging Face, vLLM, LangChain release notes
Podcasts and newsletters: Latent Space, The Batch, Import AI, Interconnects
Re-run your own evals on each new frontier model release
Maintain a personal notes system and a list of open questions
questions: What recent paper or release changed how you build agents, and why?
